 Kane gets two assists as Bayern stay top with win
 Match Summary

 Image source, EPA Image caption, Harry Kane has scored four goals in the Bundesliga this season - but has not found the net in his past three league games
 By Timothy Abraham BBC Sport Journalist Harry Kane provided two assists as Bayern Munich beat Mainz to consolidate their place at the top of the Bundesliga. 
 The 33-year-old Ballon d'Or winner teed up goals for Joshua Kimmich and Lennart Karl to take his assist tally for the season to a league-high eight - equalling his best Bundesliga total, achieved in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 campaigns.
 Kane also has more assists than any other player in the first nine matchdays of a Bundesliga season since Opta began collecting data in 2004-05.
 The England striker is on course to surpass his best tally of 14 assists in a Premier League season, which he recorded with Tottenham in the 2020-21 campaign.
 Bayern's victory left them level on 21 points with second-placed Borussia Dortmund, who beat Elversberg 2-1 at home, but the Bavarian side remain top on goal difference.
 Kimmich put the Bundesliga champions ahead in the 14th minute after Mainz defender Danny da Costa stumbled while receiving a pass from Lee Jae-sung.
 Kane seized on the loose ball and fed Kimmich, who arrowed a powerful shot from the edge of the box into the top-right corner.
 Lee thought he had equalised for Mainz when he headed in after Manuel Neuer had flapped at a free-kick towards the back post.
 However, VAR ruled the goal out for offside following a lengthy check. 
 Neuer, who became Bayern's oldest-ever Bundesliga player at 40 years and 225 days, was substituted because of injury immediately afterwards.
 Bayern added a second before the hour when Kane played the ball into the path of Karl, who swept it home from a tight angle.
 Mainz pulled a goal back in added time when Phillip Tietz glanced in a header from Benedict Hollerbach's cross, but Bayern held on to secure the points.
